label: Correct move: P.Correct m: the move m is correct by the grammar of the practice P, that is, it is…
definition: `P.Correct m`: the move m (an affirmation, confession or condemnation made in the practice) is correct by the grammar of the practice P, that is, it is a move the practice's rules make right, not merely one some participant makes.
note: Analytical vocabulary for the fideist bundle (#1010): 'grammar' in the Wittgensteinian sense the SEP entries report. It fixes no theory of what makes a move correct; the internal-grammar thesis supplies one direction.

formal_gap.meaning: Practice.Correct m says that the move m (an affirmation, confession or condemnation made in the practice) is correct by the practice's grammar: the practice's rules make it right, not merely that some participant makes it. 'Grammar' is meant in the Wittgensteinian sense the SEP entries report. It is a field of a religious practice viewed as a language game (TruthCore.Alternatives.Fideism, #1010), supplied by each model.
examples: Confessing the creed's 'one God, the Father almighty' in the Catholic practice, as a move its rules make right.
exclusions: A move some participant makes that the rules do not license.

Answerability to standards of reason shared with those outside the practice: the separate predicate AnswersToSharedReason. Neither predicate represents the external truth of a move's content, which would need its own predicate and bridge.
open_obligations: No theory of what makes a move correct is fixed; the internal-grammar thesis STMT-WF-RELIGION-INTERNAL-GRAMMAR (OwnStandard m → Correct m) supplies only one direction, and it is an open fideist commitment.
No formalization candidate from existing vocabulary.
